newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still off late on weather, charts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still off late on weather, charts.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained lower late Wednesday in lackluster trade, still undermined by milder East Coast and Midwest weather forecasts and technical selling after Tuesday's weak close.
At 1445 EDT, August skidded 4.4 cents to $2.066 per million British thermal units, while September was 3.7 cents lower at $2.076. Other deferreds were down by 0.1 to 3.7 cents.

"Temperatures are moderating enough in northern states that I think you'll see more gas on the market Monday which could soften the cash," said one Texas-based trader, adding the technicals turned more bearish after Tuesday's slide.
Cooler air is expected to arrive later this week in the East and Midwest, according to Weather Services Corp, which should keep the cash on the defensive near-term.
But traders said steady injection demand and continued heat next week in Texas and the Southwest could limit the slide.
A Reuter poll of industry players showed most expected a weekly AGA stock build of 85-95 bcf versus a 93 bcf gain last year.

Chart traders agreed August's dip Tuesday below trendline support helped trigger some early long liquidation and technical selling. Support was now seen at $2.055, the spot continuation low on June 12, with further buying likely at $2. Resistance remained first at $2.15 and then along the down trendline at $2.27. Further selling was likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.

In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast prices slipped a few cents to about the $2.10 level. Midcon pipes were down slightly in the $2.02-2.03 area. New York city gate gas was quoted three to four cents lower in the high-$2.30s.
NYMEX said 22,634 contracts traded at 1415 EDT.
NYMEX natgas trade will close at 1300 EDT Thursday ahead of the Independence Day holiday.
On the KCBT, August was still down by 1.2 cents at $1.97, while deferreds were steady to 0.9 cent lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.2 cents to 9.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
